rationale: This is essentially the archived "Current-Debt-Covered Profit" with dlc swapped for dltt and a three-year cash-flow sum, i.e., the same profitability × cash-coverage-of-debt bottleneck rather than a substantively new mechanism, and the flow-minus-stock leg is dominated by the well-known low-leverage and operating-cash-flow-to-assets effects.

Very close to the archived "Liquid-Claim-Covered EBITDA Margin" (margin × liquid-claim coverage) with a difference-form buffer instead of a ratio, and it double-counts leverage because pretax margin already subtracts interest expense while the second leg re-penalizes funded debt.

The coverage leg is copied verbatim from an archived signal and the profit-count leg is the classic Piotroski/quality "years profitable" screen, which as a 0–5 integer produces massive rank ties and lumpy, unstable portfolio composition.

Pairing a profitability trend with a deleveraging trend is a defensible and internally consistent departure from the archive's level-profitability × debt-change signals, though the debt-trend leg substantially overlaps the published net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly and three-point TREND estimates will be noisy.

The sign flip on SG&A is properly motivated by the archive's contrary evidence and "profitable despite heavy SG&A" is a coherent organization-capital screen, but it leans on a known intangible-investment anomaly and the triple-MIN structure repeats a construction that previously delivered near-zero alpha and thin coverage.

The ABS in the denominator breaks the stated economics—deeply loss-making firms with large negative OIBDP receive a low "fragility" score and are excluded from the short leg—so the expression contradicts the hypothesis, and what remains is largely capital intensity plus leverage, i.e., a repackaged distress/asset-heaviness effect.
